title: MTTR baseline + targets (Incident Bot v2 diagnostics) — working sheet
content:
Purpose
- Establish an MTTR baseline by incident class (last 90 days) and set targets for Incident Bot v2 diagnostics rollout.
- Define measurement method, segmentation, and experiment design for beta cohort.

Definitions (working)
- Incident classes: categories used for analysis and to pick the “right” diagnostic context (deploy/config/saturation).
- MTTR (primary): time from incident declared (Slack #incidents “Incident opened” / PagerDuty trigger, whichever earlier) to mitigation applied (first action that returns SLO burn to normal, or customer-visible impact ends).
- TTT (supporting): time-to-triage = time from incident declared to “likely cause” identified (deploy regression, misconfig, capacity/saturation, unknown).
- Time-to-first-mitigation step (supporting): time from incident declared to first mitigation action (rollback, flag disable, reroute, capacity shift).
- Context completeness score (supporting): percent of incidents where bot posts the 3 required cards within 90s: Deploy Context + Config Diff (redacted) + Saturation Signals.

Data sources (baseline)
- Incident timeline: #incidents channel message timestamps + PagerDuty incident lifecycle (where available).
- Mitigation marker: commander/IC notes in thread + PD “resolved” notes + change record (rollback/flag change).
- Class label: postmortem tags when available; otherwise manual classification from incident thread summary.
- Sampling window: 2024-11-10 to 2025-02-10 (rolling 90d). NOTE: still validating completeness for EU incidents.

Baseline summary (90d)
Assumptions:
- Only Sev0/Sev1/Sev2 included in this rollup; Sev3 excluded (too noisy, inconsistent timelines).
- Multiple mitigations: use first mitigation that materially reduces customer impact.
- If incident reopened: treat as separate incident only if a new PD incident exists; otherwise extend end time.

Table A — Baseline MTTR by incident class (minutes)
Columns: N | P50 MTTR | P75 MTTR | P90 MTTR | Median TTT | Dominant missing context (qualitative)

1) Deploy regressions (hosted API + control plane)
- N: 14
- P50 MTTR: 41
- P75 MTTR: 69
- P90 MTTR: 122
- Median TTT: 13
- Missing context: “what shipped where” (service version/rollout phase), canary health, commit/PR linkage

2) Config / routing / quota misconfig (tenant-safe)
- N: 11
- P50 MTTR: 58
- P75 MTTR: 94
- P90 MTTR: 165
- Median TTT: 21
- Missing context: safe diff of routing policy + feature flags; hard to confirm partial propagation/rollback status

3) Regional capacity / saturation (GPU pools, queue depth)
- N: 9
- P50 MTTR: 47
- P75 MTTR: 82
- P90 MTTR: 141
- Median TTT: 18
- Missing context: consistent saturation signals (GPU util vs queue vs KV pressure), clear links to dashboards by region/pool

4) Streaming timeouts / disconnects (multi-causal)
- N: 8
- P50 MTTR: 64
- P75 MTTR: 101
- P90 MTTR: 186
- Median TTT: 26
- Missing context: correlation between deploy + config + saturation; responders do manual log/tracing pivots

5) Third-party / upstream dependency (cloud provider / auth / networking)
- N: 6
- P50 MTTR: 55
- P75 MTTR: 88
- P90 MTTR: 130
- Median TTT: 19
- Missing context: not primarily a bot issue; value is in fast elimination (show “no deploy/config change; saturation normal”) + deep links

6) Unknown / mixed / insufficient evidence
- N: 7
- P50 MTTR: 73
- P75 MTTR: 118
- P90 MTTR: 210
- Median TTT: 31
- Missing context: everything; lack of standardized first-5-min evidence

Baseline aggregate (Sev0–Sev2)
- N total: 55
- P50 MTTR: 52
- P75 MTTR: 91
- P90 MTTR: 168
- Notes: biggest tail drivers are (a) misconfig confirmation + partial propagation and (b) saturation incidents requiring manual dashboard hopping.

Targets (Q1/Q2 2025)
Primary success criterion (beta → GA):
- Reduce P50 MTTR by incident class where bot v2 has direct leverage (deploy regression, config misconfig, saturation) without increasing incident load or telemetry query costs.

Table B — Target MTTR reductions by incident class (beta expectations)
Columns: Baseline P50 | Target P50 | Delta | Rationale

1) Deploy regressions
- Baseline P50: 41
- Target P50: 30
- Delta: -11 min (-27%)
- Rationale: instant deploy timeline + canary health + “rollback now” confidence; fewer manual release lookups.

2) Config / routing / quota misconfig
- Baseline P50: 58
- Target P50: 40
- Delta: -18 min (-31%)
- Rationale: redacted config diff + propagation/rollout hints; faster revert/disable of offending flags/policies.

3) Regional capacity / saturation
- Baseline P50: 47
- Target P50: 35
- Delta: -12 min (-26%)
- Rationale: normalized saturation card + deep links; quicker decision: shift traffic, enable fallback variant, request capacity, adjust batching.

4) Streaming timeouts / disconnects
- Baseline P50: 64
- Target P50: 54
- Delta: -10 min (-16%)
- Rationale: earlier correlation hypothesis; still multi-causal and depends on tracing/log hygiene.

Non-targeted / “should not regress”
- Third-party dependency: keep P50 within ±5 min; success is faster elimination and fewer wrong mitigations.
- Unknown/mixed: aim -10% as a lagging indicator via improved evidence capture.

Secondary targets (diagnostics quality + safety)
- Context completeness score (within 90s of incident open in #incidents):
  - Baseline (current bot): Deploy 35% | Config diff 0–5% (ad hoc) | Saturation 42% | All three 18%
  - Beta target: Deploy 80% | Config diff 60% | Saturation 80% | All three 55%
  - GA target: Deploy 90% | Config diff 80% | Saturation 90% | All three 75%
- Bot response time (p95 time-to-first-card):
  - Target: <= 15s for first card; <= 60s for all cards; degraded mode triggers at 10s upstream timeout per card.
- Telemetry query guardrails:
  - Per-incident query budget: cap at 25 queries (aggregated); enforce caching + coalescing; hard timeout on high-cardinality fallbacks.
- Safety:
  - Zero P0 privacy incidents: no secret leakage in Slack output; audit logs for config diff + privileged telemetry access.

Measurement plan
What we will measure (per incident):
- MTTR (minutes) with consistent start/end markers (see Definitions).
- TTT (minutes) and time-to-first-mitigation step.
- Context completeness score + time-to-context (deploy/config/sat each).
- Bot diagnostics health: error rate, timeouts, degraded mode count, cache hit rate.
- Operator actions: whether incident used bot interactive actions (expand diff, open dashboard links, copy commands) — proxy for adoption.

Segmentation (for analysis)
- Severity: Sev0/Sev1/Sev2.
- Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated pools vs private (where applicable).
- Region: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (initial).
- Incident class: deploy vs config vs saturation vs streaming vs third-party vs unknown.
- Cohort: beta rotation vs non-beta (see experiment design).

Experiment design (beta rollout)
Goal: estimate impact on MTTR while controlling for severity mix and avoiding bot-induced load.

Design (quasi-experimental, staged rollout)
- Phase 0 (pre-beta, 2 weeks): instrumentation only
  - Ensure bot logs can compute completeness and response times.
  - Validate audit events and redaction tests.
- Phase 1 (beta cohort, 2 weeks): enable v2 cards for SRE primary rotation only
  - Cohort definition: SRE on-call rotation in #incidents + #eng-oncall; target 10–15 incidents.
  - Regions: us-east-1 + eu-west-1 (to test regional data availability).
- Phase 2 (expanded beta, 2 weeks): add platform on-call + telemetry on-call
  - Add more incident types; stress test query budgets.
- Phase 3 (GA candidate): broaden to all engineering responders

Control approach
- Not a pure randomized experiment (incidents not random). Use difference-in-differences:
  - Compare beta period vs pre-beta for the same incident classes, severity, and region.
  - Compare to non-beta responders/time windows when v2 disabled (feature flag cohorting).
- Adjust for severity mix by reporting within-class deltas and using severity-weighted aggregates.

Sample size / power (rough)
- We expect ~10–20 Sev0–Sev2 incidents per 2-week window.
- Primary readout: directionally meaningful reduction in P50 and shift in tail (P90) for targeted classes.
- We will treat beta as “evidence + safety gate,” not a publishable experiment.

Success gates for GA
- Safety: no redaction regressions; audit logs present for 100% of privileged calls.
- Performance: bot p95 first-card <= 15s, and <5% interactions failing due to timeouts (excluding upstream outages where degraded mode is expected).
- Reliability: diagnostics endpoints do not materially worsen incidents (no self-inflicted overload; circuit breaker triggers behave as designed).
- Outcome: at least 20% P50 MTTR reduction in ≥2 of the 3 targeted classes OR clear improvement in TTT + context completeness that correlates with faster mitigation.

Operational notes / open questions
- Timestamp source of truth: prefer PagerDuty trigger for start if present; else Slack incident-open message timestamp. Need a deterministic fallback rule.
- Incident class labeling: we need a lightweight taxonomy tag in incident template to reduce manual classification.
- Dedicated/private segmentation: some incidents don’t map cleanly to a single pool/tenant; need consistent “primary impacted surface.”
- Outlier handling: large multi-hour incidents distort P90; keep but annotate “multi-wave” incidents.
- Data retention: ensure bot logs + audit logs kept long enough for Q2 readout.

Action items (as of 2025-03-06)
- Rafael Mendes: confirm baseline N and re-check EU incident completeness.
- Aisha Bello: align MTTR readout with SLO burn categories (latency vs 5xx vs streaming disconnect).
- Logan Wright: confirm telemetry query budget feasibility + metrics for cache hit rate and degraded mode.
- Connor O’Brien: validate deploy context coverage for all services (join plan gaps).
- Miles Thornton: add per-incident “context completeness” event in bot logs + export to metrics.

Changelog
- 2025-02-11: initial baseline table (rough counts) + first target proposal.
- 2025-02-24: added context completeness score + beta/GA targets.
- 2025-03-06: updated baselines for streaming and unknown classes; tightened GA gates.
